title: Narvi — Turns & Outbound Delivery
description: Turn-outcome integrity (is a turn we called Failed actually one that succeeded) and outbound-notification delivery health. Panels correspond to IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md row 77's own 'false failures' and 'outbox lag' subjects. Every metric name below is checked against the real registered OTel instruments by internal/ops's own drift test (go test ./internal/ops/...) — a panel referencing a renamed or removed metric fails that build.

panels.title: Turn false failures (rate)
panels.description: Rate of turn_false_failure_total — a late, real execution_complete{outcome:completed} arriving for a session the control plane already terminalized Failed with failure_reason=timeout. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md row 77's own 'false failures' subject: a turn_deadline expiry that turned out to be wrong — the agent was still working and actually finished. Target: ~0, mirroring §5.3's own watchdog-false-alarm framing for the same class of problem (the control plane's own inference being contradicted after the fact).

panels.title: Outbox delivery lag
panels.description: outbox_lag_seconds — age, in seconds, of the oldest still-due outbox row claimed at the start of the most recent pump tick (internal/app/outboxworker). IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md row 77's own 'outbox lag' subject; §5.3's own 'outbox lag'. Zero when nothing is due — watch this alongside outbox-due-backlog below, since this alone reads zero during a sustained outage where every pending row is mid-backoff.

panels.title: Outbox pending backlog (including mid-backoff)
panels.description: outbox_due_backlog_count — total count of 'pending' outbox rows, INCLUDING rows still mid-backoff (next_attempt_at in the future). The audit-fix companion to outbox-lag above: stays visible during a sustained outage where every pending row is currently cooling down and outbox_lag_seconds alone would misleadingly read zero.

panels.title: Outbox dead-letters (rate)
panels.description: Rate of outbox_dead_letter_total — outbox entries that exhausted domain/outbox.MaxAttempts delivery attempts and were dead-lettered. Every dead-letter is a notification (a Slack/Linear/GitHub update, a plan-approval request, ...) that a user never received.

panels.title: Auto-merge auth/permission dead-letters (rate)
panels.description: Rate of automerge_auth_dead_lettered_total — internal/app/automerge.Worker's own authGuard giving up on a scope (the shared worker-wide bot credential, or one repository) after exhausting domain/automerge.MaxAuthFailures consecutive authentication/permission-classified GitHub failures (docs/TECHNICAL_PLAN.md §17). A worker-wide dead-letter stops EVERY armed repository's own auto-merge until an operator rotates the credential and redeploys; a per-repository one stops only that repository.
